2608.26550.title: SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning
2608.26550.paper_summary: Reinforcement learning-based knowledge distillation has the potential to transfer complex reasoning from teacher to student models, yet it currently faces a critical dilemma: researchers must choose between sparse outcome-based rewards, which provide insufficient logical guidance, or expensive neural Process Reward Models (PRMs) for dense signals. We resolve this by introducing SPEAR (Symbolic Process Evaluation and Alignment Reward), a training-free and plug-and-play process reward method for sequence-level on-policy distillation. SPEAR projects natural-language reasoning traces into domain-adaptive symbolic milestones, providing an efficient proxy for process-level reasoning alignment. By utilizing the longest common subsequence (LCS) to align student explorations with teacher milestones, SPEAR provides a dense, order-aware reward signal that enforces logical consistency without the need for an external neural verifier. Our experiments across math, science, and commonsense reasoning tasks demonstrate that SPEAR effectively bridges the reasoning gap between student and teacher models via sequence-level distillation with efficient dense process rewards. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/zhuochunli/SPEAR.
2608.26550.paper_summary_zh: 基於強化學習的知識蒸餾有潛力將複雜的推理從教師模型轉移到學生模型，然而目前面臨一個關鍵的困境：研究人員必須在稀疏的基於結果的獎勵（這些獎勵提供不足的邏輯指導）和昂貴的神經過程獎勵模型（PRMs，提供密集信號）之間做出選擇。<lb/>我們通過引入SPEAR（符號過程評估與對齊獎勵）來解決這個問題，這是一種無需訓練且即插即用的過程獎勵方法，適用於序列級的策略蒸餾。<lb/>SPEAR將自然語言推理痕跡投影到領域自適應的符號里程碑，提供了一個高效的過程級推理對齊代理。<lb/>通過利用最長公共子序列（LCS）將學生的探索與教師的里程碑對齊，SPEAR提供了一個密集的、考慮順序的獎勵信號，強化邏輯一致性，而無需外部神經驗證器。<lb/>我們在數學、科學和常識推理任務中的實驗表明，SPEAR有效地縮小了學生模型與教師模型之間的推理差距，通過序列級的蒸餾和高效的密集過程獎勵。<lb/>我們的代碼和數據可在以下網址獲得：https://github.com/zhuochunli/SPEAR。
